q1_issues.issue: "No lantern went out" is stated without restriction, but the rule premise carries (On $x cliff_path) over from the previous sentence, narrowing the claim to a subset the sentence does not name.
"the lanterns OF the three bright stations" is a possessive / part-whole of-phrase, which routes to PartOf or Possession; LocatedIn asserts a spatial containment the text never states.

The per-member burn rule types its object only as (Member (sk_mire_essence $x) extra) and omits the kind atom (Member (sk_mire_essence $x) mire_essence), unlike the parallel produce rule which types its Skolem object both ways.

"crowds of nightmoths" is plural — a bare-plural episodic object should mint a group of crowds — but the parse mints one crowd witness, and the later plural "the nightmoth crowds" likewise binds to a single crowd symbol.

q2_gaps: approximate / hedged exact counts ("about thirty nightmoths") — Cardinality is specified as a native integer, and CardinalityPhrase covers only number-less vague phrases

an eventuality distributed over a counted subset of days ("on six of the next ten nights", "on those six nights") — Time admits calendar terms or deictic/named constants only, with no filler for a set-of-nights witness and no machinery to distribute the event across the occasions
a forward multi-unit temporal window ("the next ten nights") — only the backward WithinLast window and single-unit "next / following" increments are covered

a per-period count rate ("about thirty nightmoths per night") — compound per-units are licensed only in the Measure family, so a count-per-period has to borrow the habitual (Every e 1 night), which says the counting recurred rather than that the count was per night
notes: (Time <e> sk_nights_2) puts a group witness in a slot the instruction set restricts to calendar terms and deictic constants — the least-bad option given the gap above, not an invented head. The light-verb treatment of "the first cold snap came" (tense and Time straight on the event-noun witness) extends a list given as occurred / happened / took place, and reads as a faithful extension rather than a defect.
